findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: M \log_2(1 + \mathrm{SNR}/M) \propto \log(\mathrm{SNR}) \text{ as } \mathrm{SNR} \to \infty, \text{ not } O(\mathrm{SNR})\text{.} Spatial multiplexing increases the pre-log factor (degrees of freedom), so data rate scales logarithmically with SNR at high SNR, never linearly with SNR regardless of spatial multiplexing or scattering conditions; at low SNR where capacity is linear in SNR, beamforming rather than spatial multiplexing is optimal and rate does not exceed the linear wideband limit.} } } ", but more directly: Spatial multiplexing provides degrees-of-freedom gain, yielding capacity scaling C \approx \min(N_t, N_r) \log_2(\mathrm{SNR}), which is logarithmic, not linear, in SNR.

evidence.text: Peak data rate can be made to grow linearly with SNR by means of spatial multiplexing even in far field scenarios, since omni-directional transmission does not prevent rich scattering.
